title: From Rigid to Flexible: how Flawless rebuilt its people processes with Humaans
summary: "We don't have to change how we work to fit the tool, and that's one of the things that mattered most to us."
body_markdown:
Flawless builds assistive AI tools that amplify human creativity rather than replacing it - allowing Directors and Editors to refine performances in the edit and enable stories to travel across the globe. Its best known technology, TrueSync, adjusts an actor's facial movements to match new dialogue in any language, preserving performance and authenticity.


Rebekah Thompson joined Flawless three years ago, when the company was around 70 people with no People systems to speak of. "We just had an HRIS plus a Google Drive with some policies and contracts in it," she says. Since then, the business has grown considerably, and her role has grown with it: building a performance framework, a feedback culture, and support for managers, largely from scratch.


> "The flexibility is on the system, not on us. We don't have to change how we work to fit the tool, and that's one of the things that mattered most to us."


Rebekah Thompson, Head of People, Flawless


## **Flawless at a glance**


- **Sector:** Assistive AI tools for Film,TV and Advertising
- **Headquarters:** London, UK
- **Additional locations:** Los Angeles, US, plus distributed contractors
- **HR tech stack:** Humaans, Claude (via MCP), Zinc, Slack, Rippling


## **Key results**


- Replaced a rigid, one-size-fits-all performance system with a fully customisable platform the People team can adapt in minutes
- Turned a manual, broken-link probation approval process into a smooth digital workflow with clear, sequential sign-off
- Built a Claude and Humaans MCP integration that automatically notifies new managers with next steps, set up once in around 20 minutes
- One consistent platform experience across UK and US teams, with no region-specific limitations
- Ongoing input into the Humaans product roadmap, with feedback regularly acted on


## **Outgrowing a rigid, one-size-fits-all platform**


By the time Rebekah set out to change Flawless’'s HR systems, the business had already outgrown its original tools. "HiBob was just a bit clunky," she says. "It was a bit old school, and it wasn’t always intuitive."


The bigger, ongoing frustration was with how little the platform could flex to Flawless’s way of working.


> "It wasn't always customisable, and that was probably the biggest thing," Rebekah explains. When managers needed to raise a performance issue during someone's probation, the process depended on a document link that had to be copied and pasted manually, and frequently didn't work. "We'd end up manually starting an email chain to get it approved. It was quite manual, and we found that was the case with a lot of things."


As an assistive AI company, Flawless also holds itself to a high bar on how AI is used responsibly, which made a particular issue with Workleap’sAI features hard to ignore.


> "I remember going into a review with someone on my team, and it had summarised that this person was really good at organising events. I had no idea where that came from. It turned out to be a shout-out from a year earlier for a social event, and it had turned that into a strength" she says. "It did that quite often: pulling things together and making words up. Given how much we care about using AI responsibly, that made a lot of people uncomfortable."


Support didn't help matters. "At Bob, we didn’t speak to a customer success manager the entire time we were there, until we decided to terminate one of the modules.” Rebekah says.


Not every AI tool had earned Flawless AI's trust either. A dedicated AI-for-HR platform, Workleap, had proved unreliable in practice, and commitments made along the way weren't followed through on: "we encountered bugs in the system every month we were with them, to the point where we only considered one of the features usable."


## **Choosing a partner that would flex around the business, not the other way around**


When the search for a replacement began, Flawless looked at Humaans alongside a couple of other providers. What set the conversation with Humaans apart, even before a decision was made, was how directly the team engaged with what Flawless actually needed.


> "They were really transparent and honest about what the platform could do and what it couldn't," Rebekah says. “They'd tell us clearly when something would be ready, and if it wasn't locked in yet, they'd still give us a realistic timeline rather than a vague promise. We're both quite relationship-driven, and we wanted to actually work with the company we chose, not just buy a product from them."


The Humaans team also visited Flawless on site to understand their processes directly. "They were genuinely trying to understand the problems we had, which we thought was really nice."


Customizability was the deciding factor. "We liked that it was an evolving, changing product. We could give feedback and actually work with Humaans on it," she says. That stood in sharp contrast to her experience elsewhere. "I felt like HiBob and Workleap would tell us we couldn't do something, meaning we'd have to change our process to fit their system. That's a terrible response. With Humaans, we know we can build a way to do what we want, even if it's an edge case."


## **A smooth migration onto one flexible platform**


The migration off HiBob was handled largely by Rebekah's colleague Tessa, and by her account it was far more straightforward than expected. "We thought it was going to be a slog, and it really wasn't," Rebekah says. Uploading historical documents, in particular, stood out. "She just uploaded them and the Humaans system figured out who they belonged to. Now everything, every performance conversation, every document, is in one place."


That single source of truth has changed the day-to-day considerably. Quarterly reflections, for example, are now lightweight by design. "We ask a couple of core questions and one optional one, and when we want to change the questions, it's very easy to do," Rebekah says. She points to the same probation workflow that used to rely on broken links and manual email chains as one of the clearest improvements. "Now it's a proper workflow. The form, the video, everything is accessible from my inbox. It's set up so multiple people can approve at once, then it moves to the next step. That kind of thing genuinely wasn't possible before."


The platform has also proven equally flexible across Flawless's UK and US teams.


> "It doesn't feel like there's any difference. There aren't any quirks where something is set up for UK employees that wouldn't apply in the US," she says. "It feels just as well designed for a US employee as it does for someone in the UK."


Feedback into the Humaans roadmap has been a highlight since the switch. Rebekah points to the engagement survey feature as a direct result of conversations her team had with Humaans about what they needed, and colleagues have had smaller pieces of feedback, such as making it easier to find someone's performance history once a task has closed, acknowledged and picked up quickly. "It doesn't go into a void," she says.


## **Building AI-native workflows with Claude and the Humaans MCP**


As a technology company, Flawless has naturally pushed to bring automation into their people processes, and then into how it uses Humaans. Rebekah recently connected the Humaans MCP to Claude to solve a small but persistent gap in how new managers were supported.


> "Claude checks Humaans daily for anyone who's become a manager for the first time," she explains. "When it finds one, it sends them a Slack message from me directly, letting them know they're now managing someone, and also to them letting them know what they need to do next."


What struck her most was how little effort it took.


> "The connection between Claude and Humaans was so easy and seamless, it honestly felt like magic. I set it up once, in about twenty minutes, and now it just fires off automatically."


She's planning to extend the same approach to a redesigned peer feedback process, where the MCP will check whether an employee has chosen to include their manager before routing the feedback accordingly.


## **A platform built to flex as Flawless scales**


For a company whose product is built on constant experimentation, Rebekah sees that same flexibility as the defining reason Humaans has worked for Flawless. "It's customisable, so for a team that's changing and experimenting, you can set something up quickly, try it, and just as easily throw it out or change it," she says. "The flexibility is on the system, not on us. We don't have to change how we work to fit the tool, and that's one of the things that mattered most to us.”
